what: The Sales Tax Calculator adds tax to a price or takes tax out of a total. Type an amount and a tax rate, then choose whether the amount is before tax or already includes tax. You see the price before tax, the tax itself and the price with tax.

Shoppers use it to know the real price at the till. Small business owners use it to add tax to invoices or to find the tax part of a receipt. It works for sales tax, VAT, GST or any other tax that is a simple percent of the price.
The calculation runs in your browser as you type. Results are estimates and not financial advice.
uses: Add your local tax rate to a shelf price before you buy.
Find the tax in a receipt
Switch to "Tax included (remove tax)" to split a total into the net price and the tax.
Work out the tax line and the total for a customer invoice.
Remove VAT or GST from a price that already includes it.
Try different rates to see how much tax changes the price.
tutorial: Enter a price in "Amount", for example 100. Nothing is shown until you also enter a rate.
Enter the percent in "Tax rate (%)", for example 8.25. Do not type the % sign. A rate of 0 is allowed.
In "The amount is", choose "Before tax (add tax)" if the price does not include tax yet. Choose "Tax included (remove tax)" if the price is a total that already has tax in it.
"Price before tax" is the net price, "Tax" is the tax amount, and "Price with tax" is the full total. All are rounded to 2 decimals.
Results update as soon as you edit the amount, the rate or the option.
features: Price with tax = amount × (1 + rate ÷ 100). Tax = price with tax − amount.
Price before tax = total ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100). This is the correct way; simply taking the rate off the total gives the wrong answer.
Use it for sales tax, VAT, GST or any flat percent.
Net price, tax and gross price side by side.
No button to press; numbers change while you type.

example.title: Worked example: adding and removing 8.25% tax
example.text: A jacket costs 50 before tax and the rate is 8.25%. With "Before tax (add tax)", the tool shows Price before tax 50.00, Tax 4.13 and Price with tax 54.13, because 50 × 1.0825 = 54.125. Now take a receipt total of 108.25 at the same rate and choose "Tax included (remove tax)". The tool divides 108.25 by 1.0825 and shows Price before tax 100.00 and Tax 8.25. Note that 8.25% of 108.25 would be 8.93, which is why you divide instead.

tips: Look up your combined rate; many places add city or county tax to the state rate.
To remove tax, always use the "Tax included" option instead of subtracting the percent.
The tool rounds to 2 decimals; shops may round each item separately, so totals can differ by a cent.
For a 0% rate the tax is 0 and both prices are the same.
Use the same tool for VAT by typing your VAT rate, such as 20.
problems: Both "Amount" and "Tax rate (%)" must be filled in, and the amount must be above 0.
The tax is a little different from my receipt
Shops may round tax per item or use a slightly different rate. Check the exact rate printed on the receipt.
I removed tax and got a strange number
Make sure the option says "Tax included (remove tax)" and that you typed the total that already includes tax.
A negative rate gives no result
Tax rates must be 0 or more.
